t: Minimum Moves to Equal Array Elements III
o: Only increments are allowed, so every element must rise to the maximum. In [2,1,3] the target is 3 and the cost is 1+2+0 = 3; in [4,4,5] the target is 5 costing 1+1 = 2. Any target below the max is unreachable and any target above wastes moves, so the answer is sum(nums) - n * max(nums). Constraints (n, values ≤ 100) make anything work, but the formula is O(n).
k: Increments-only forces the final value to be max(nums).

a.i: Each element nums[i] needs exactly max - nums[i] increments; summing gives sum - n*max. No simulation required.
s: Compute mx = max(nums) and total = sum(nums).
a.t: O(n) — one pass for sum and max

w: Contrast with the classic LeetCode 453 where a move increments n-1 elements (equivalent to decrementing one, answer relative to the min). Here increments apply to one element, so the max governs. Pitfall: using min instead of max. Follow-up: allow both increments and decrements (then aim for the median).
